# Clash Court

> An AI war-room that builds a music festival timetable so fans do not have to choose between two acts they love.
> Qloo's taste graph scores how much every pair of acts on the bill shares fans; code builds the timetable that keeps
> those pairs apart within the booker's rules; language-model agents read the booker's plain-word orders and explain
> every move. Entry for the Qloo Agentic Hackathon 2026 by Athmeeya M Kashyap and Siddhant Gudwani. MIT licence.

## What it does

- Loads a festival day: stages, real set times and the published timetable.
- Matches every act to a Qloo artist (exact names only, never guessed); acts Qloo lacks fall back to Last.fm
  listening data, labelled as such.
- Asks Qloo how much each pair of acts shares fans, for the whole bill. Clash = shared fans times minutes of overlap.
- Moves sets between existing slots to cut clashes, keeping the rules: headliners close, no act moves more than two
  hours from its billed time, set lengths stay the same, locked stages stay locked, plus any rule the booker adds.
- A booker agent turns orders such as "Mitski just cancelled" or "Doechii arrives at 3pm" into checked rules. Fan
  agents argue for their acts with Qloo's numbers. A referee makes each move and explains it.
- A fan names up to five artists they love; Qloo scores every act on the bill for them and the page plans their best
  path through the day, flagging the clashes they cannot avoid. Those reports weigh the next re-plan.

## Ask the court (conversational agent)

A tool-using loop: the model chooses among timetable, where_is, shares_fans_with, clash_between, booker_order,
fan_route, city_plan, promoter_portfolio, promoters and evidence; code runs them; every number in the answer is
checked against the tool results and unmatched numbers are flagged. Endpoint: POST /api/clash/ask (server-sent events).

## How Qloo is used

- `/search` (artist) to resolve each act by exact name.
- `/v2/insights` with `filter.type=urn:entity:artist`, one act as `signal.interests.entities` and the rest of the bill
  in `filter.results.entities`: the pair overlap table (about one call per act, cached).
- The same endpoint with a fan's favourites as the signal: the fan's fit for every act on the bill (one call).

## Where a model alone falls short (shown on the page)

Asked the same question twice with no Qloo, a frontier model's pair scores move between answers (on a 40-act test
bill, 144 of 780 pairs moved by 10 points or more; on the real Lollapalooza Sunday, 13 of 903). Qloo returns the same
scores every time for every act it holds. On coverage the model is not worse: on that Sunday it claimed to know 9
acts Qloo lacks. Whether Qloo or the model matches real fans better is being tested (pre-registered Test 28).

## Honest limits

- Qloo does not hold every act: on the four Lollapalooza 2026 days it matched 24 to 29 of 43 acts by exact name
  (new breakout acts and small early sets lag its catalogue); on Thursday Aug 1, 2024 (the default day) 38 of 44.
  For acts Qloo lacks, fan overlap comes from Last.fm's real listening data (artist.getsimilar match, used directly
  as the weight), shown on the page as "Last.fm" with a dotted outline. With both, every act has data on every day
  except one local showcase act (Chicago Made). Last.fm matches by name too, so a generic name can land on a
  different artist (2026 Saturday's "Ink" returns drum and bass neighbours and may be the wrong act).
  The fan route still scores only acts Qloo holds.
- Qloo's raw affinity scores are bunched (unrelated acts and near-twins score close together), so each act's scores are
  ranked against the rest of the bill before use.
- A real timetable has reasons a score cannot see (contracts, production, travel). The booker states them as rules;
  the tool never claims its plan is final.
- Every claim the team tests is pre-registered before data is seen; see the PREREGISTRATION files and PROJECT_LOG.md.

## Code

- [clash/overlap.py](clash/overlap.py): festival files, Qloo matching, the pair table and clash weights
- [clash/schedule.py](clash/schedule.py): clash score on real set times, rules, optimiser
- [clash/agents.py](clash/agents.py): booker command reader, fan agents, referee
- [clash/fanroute.py](clash/fanroute.py): a fan's best path through the day
- [clash/baseline.py](clash/baseline.py): the model-alone comparison
- [clash/api.py](clash/api.py), [static/clash.html](static/clash.html): the web app
- [tests/test_clash_schedule.py](tests/test_clash_schedule.py): engine tests
